commits.message: Markdown image review: pin Rich 15's inline HTML, plain exit steps, docs line in words (rich-unfiled-791c.vke3)

Markdown draws an image ahead of its block, linked to an enclosing link, as Rich does (rich-unfiled-791c.vke3)

Rich's render loop draws an image the moment it meets one, ahead of the
top-level block holding it, and links the alt text to the link it sits in.
A list is now one token, so an image in any item is drawn ahead of the
whole list.

Markdown pairs * and _ emphasis by markdown-it's flanking rules, as Rich does (rich-unfiled-791c.ljiy) (#429)

* Markdown pairs * and _ emphasis by markdown-it's flanking rules, as Rich does (rich-unfiled-791c.ljiy)

Emphasis was found by scanning forward for a closing *, which knew nothing
of _, of flanking, or of the rule of 3. The scan now records each * or _
run as a delimiter whose can-open and can-close are read once from what
borders it (scanDelims), pairs them in markdown-it's balance_pairs pass,
and makes strong and em from the pairs as its emphasis postProcess does.
A link's label is read from the block's own text up to its ], so its
delimiters see what precedes them and pair only with each other.

* Markdown reads each line ending in the inline pass, as markdown-it does (rich-unfiled-791c.ljiy)

The block pass decided hard breaks and dropped a break's backslash before
the inline pass ran, so a delimiter run before `\`+newline read whitespace
where markdown-it's scanDelims reads punctuation, and `x\\` at a line's end
broke hard where markdown-it escapes the backslash. Paragraph lines now
join at their line endings; the inline pass reads each as markdown-it's
newline and escape rules do, which also gives a code span's line ending
as a space and an image's alt its newline, as Rich draws them.

* Markdown reads a line ending by the text before it, as markdown-it's newline rule does (rich-unfiled-791c.ljiy)

Matching a line ending ahead from every space scanned each run of spaces
once per space; 100k spaces took over four seconds. The line ending is now
the construct, and the spaces ending the pending text decide soft or hard.
